title: Group schemes over a field have a unique irreducible component through the identity, geometrically irreducible

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: every point of G is hit by a K-rational point of G_K and the local ring map is faithfully flat, so the unique-minimal-prime statement reduces to rational points; at a rational point g translation is an automorphism carrying e to g, so all local rings at rational points agree with O_{G,e} and (2) implies (1); for (2) over an algebraically closed field, two components Z_1, Z_2 through e have irreducible product Z_1 x_k Z_2, whose image under multiplication contains both Z_1 and Z_2 (restriction of m to the axes is the identity), forcing Z_1 = Z_2; geometric irreducibility of Z follows since the argument applies over any field extension (source lines 1015-1046)

core_obligations: Reduction to rational points (proof lines 1016-1026): every g is hit by a K-rational point of G_K; O_{G,g} -> O_{G_K,g'} is faithfully flat local (00HR), so the minimal-prime uniqueness descends (00FK).
(2) implies (1) (proof lines 1027-1033): translation by a rational point g is an automorphism mapping e to g, so O_{G,g} = O_{G,e}, and components through e correspond to minimal primes of O_{G,e}.

Uniqueness and geometric irreducibility (proof lines 1035-1046): over k-bar, Z_1 x_k Z_2 is irreducible (038F); its image under m contains both Z_1 and Z_2 since m|_{e x G} = m|_{G x e} = id, so any component containing the image contains both, whence Z_1 = Z_2; the same reasoning over each K/k gives (3).
proof_roadmap: Reduce (1) to rational points via faithful flatness (proof lines 1016-1026).
Identify all rational-point local rings with O_{G,e} by translation (proof lines 1027-1033).
Prove uniqueness of the component through e over k-bar and conclude geometric irreducibility (proof lines 1035-1046).
